We present useful results from luripotential theory to prove weak convergence of the normalized Bergman kernel.

**Definition 34.** Let \(\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n\) be a domain and \(p \in b\Omega\). We say that \(\Omega\) is **Bergman exhaustive** at \(p\) if \(\lim_{z\to p} K(z,z)=\infty\).

If \(\Omega\) is Bergman exhaustive at every boundary point, we say that \(\Omega\) is Bergman exhaustive.

**Definition 35.** Let \(\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n\) be a domain and fix \(a \in \Omega\). The **pluricomplex Green function** of \(\Omega\) with pole at \(w\) is defined by

\[
g_{\Omega}(\cdot,w)=\sup\left\{u(\cdot):u\in PSH^{-}(\Omega),\limsup_{z\to w}\big(u(z)-\log|z-w|\big)<\infty\right\},
\]

where \(PSH^{-}(\Omega)\) denotes the set of all negative plurisubharmonic functions on \(\Omega\).

For an arbitrary domain \(\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n\) and a point \(z \in \Omega\), define

\[
\Gamma_z=\left\{w\in\Omega:g_{\Omega}(z,w)<\frac{1}{e}\right\}.
\]

**Theorem 14.** \([JP13,\ \text{Theorem }12.4.2]\) Let \(\Omega\) be a pseudoconvex domain in \(\mathbb{C}^n\) and \(p \in b\Omega\). Assume that

\[
\lim_{z\to p} V(\Gamma_z)=0.
\]

Then, \(\Omega\) is Bergman exhaustive.

The next results show that for a bounded hyperconvex domain \(\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n\), we have weak convergence of the normalized Bergman kernel \(k_z\) as \(z \in \Omega\) approaches a boundary point.

1. Introduction. Let D be a bounded pseudoconvex domain in Cn with
a smooth boundary. We will investigate the behavior of the pluricomplex
Green function GD(·, w), w ∈D, of D when w tends to the boundary.
This function is deﬁned by
GD(·, w) := sup{u(z) | u ∈P(w; D)},
where P(w; D) denotes the class of all negative plurisubharmonic functions
on D such that u −log | · −w| is bounded from above near w. It has been
introduced by Klimek [Kli1], and later in hyperconvex domains in general
complex manifolds by Demailly [Dem]. In both papers fundamental proper-
ties of GD were proved (in particular its relationship to the Monge–Ampère
operator was clariﬁed in [Dem]).

haves when w tends to the boundary. First results in this context were ob-
tained in [CCW], [He], and [DiHe] (for quantitative results in special cases
see [Car], [Che]).
